name: Angkor Archaeological Park
tagline: The largest religious monument in the world, set among a forest of temples built by the Khmer Empire.
highlight: Watching the towers of Angkor Wat emerge from the dark at sunrise.
shortDescription: A UNESCO World Heritage Site covering over 400 square kilometres, with Angkor Wat, the faces of the Bayon, the jungle-wrapped Ta Prohm and dozens of other temples.
metaDescription: An Angkor Archaeological Park guide: Angkor Wat, the Bayon, Ta Prohm, Angkor Thom, Phnom Bakheng, tickets and passes, sunrise tips, tuk-tuks, a three-day plan and etiquette.
nearestAirport: Siem Reap-Angkor International (SAI), about 45 minutes from the temples
intro: Angkor was the capital of the Khmer Empire, which ruled much of South-East Asia from the 9th to the 15th century. The temples left behind are the largest religious monuments in the world, spread across forest and rice fields near Siem Reap, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Angkor Wat, built in the early 12th century for King Suryavarman II, is the most famous, a vast temple mountain with five towers, a moat and miles of carved bas-reliefs. A few kilometres north, Angkor Thom was the last capital, and its Bayon temple is crowned by hundreds of serene stone faces. Ta Prohm is left half-swallowed by silk-cotton and strangler fig trees.

The temples are best visited over two or three days, beginning at dawn to see the light and avoid the heat. Tuk-tuk drivers act as guides and drivers, and a three-day or seven-day pass covers the park. Modest dress is required, with shoulders and knees covered, and the area can be crowded, especially at sunrise.
